IEEE ICC 2026 · Glasgow International Conference on Communications

IEEE ICC 2026 IEEE ComSoc Flagship 5G / Beyond 5G Generative AI May 2026
Paper Presentation: Drift-Aware Conditional Diffusion Generative AI for Resource Management in 5G and Beyond Networks
IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC 2026)  ·  24–28 May 2026  ·  Glasgow, Scotland, UK  ·  Connected World for Sustainable Future
Dr. Henna presented her research paper at IEEE ICC 2026, one of the IEEE Communications Society's two flagship conferences, attended by close to 3,000 researchers and engineers from over 70 countries. The paper addresses a critical challenge in next-generation networks: concept drift — the gradual shift in traffic and network condition distributions that degrades machine learning-based resource management. The proposed two-stage framework, CondDiffTFormer + DART-ConvNet, combines a Conditional Diffusion Transformer GAN for service-aware time-series synthesis with a dilated temporal convolutional forecasting network. Evaluated on a B5G dataset spanning video streaming, URLLC emergency services, and IoT telemetry, the approach outperforms TimeGAN and TimeTransformerGAN on RMSE and MAE. This work represents a significant contribution to AI-native, drift-resilient resource allocation for 5G and Beyond 5G radio access networks.
Paper Abstract
The advancement of 5G and the emergence of Beyond 5G (B5G) networks have introduced increased service heterogeneity and dynamic traffic patterns, creating new challenges for resource allocation in radio access networks (RANs). This paper presents a service-aware approach to resource allocation under drift conditions, integrating conditional generative modelling with temporal forecasting via a two-stage framework: a Conditional Diffusion Transformer GAN (CondDiffTFormer) and a forecasting network based on dilated temporal convolutions (DART-ConvNet). The generative component synthesises time-series data conditioned on application type, using a diffusion process embedded in a transformer backbone to model long-range temporal dependencies and service-specific dynamics. Comparative results show improved generalisation, forecasting accuracy, and responsiveness to drift over TimeGAN and TimeTransformerGAN.

WeSTEMEU · Interreg Europe Study Visit, Policy Presentations & Steering Group Meetings

WeSTEMEUPolicy InstrumentInterreg Europe
WeSTEMEU 7th Steering Group Meeting & Study Visit, Igualada
January 2025 · Campus Igualada, University of Lleida, Spain
The 7th Steering Group Meeting of the WeSTEMEU project was held at the University of Lleida (UdL), Campus Igualada, bringing together 19 representatives from partner institutions. Dr. Henna presented the Policy Improvement approved within the Interreg Europe framework on behalf of Atlantic Technological University (Ireland), highlighting how interregional learning has contributed to concrete policy changes integrating gender equality and STEM priorities. Special recognition was given to both the Podkarpackie Region (Poland) and ATU (Ireland) for leading approved policy improvements. Topics included monitoring, financial status, the follow-up phase, and preparation for the Final Conference in Brussels.

ARC Hub for ICT — Official Launch
Research Ireland · Co-funded by Government of Ireland & European Union via ERDF
Dr. Henna attended the official launch of the ARC Hub for ICT as a co-applicant and Principal Investigator leading three projects within the Hub. The Hub fills a critical funding and support gap in Ireland's Innovation Ecosystem, accelerating the translation of ICT research into industry-ready solutions.
ARC Hub for ICTResearch IrelandPrincipal Investigator6G · IoT · AI
ARC Hub for ICT — Accelerating Research to Commercialisation
Research Ireland · Co-funded by Government of Ireland & European Union (ERDF) · Southern Regional Assembly
Dr. Henna is a Principal Investigator within the ARC Hub for ICT, leading three research projects focused on AI commercialisation, technology validation, and industry adoption. The Hub bridges academic AI research and real-world industry deployment in telecommunications, digital infrastructure, and intelligent systems.

Research projects led by Dr. Henna within the Hub include: 6GOrch (Low-Variance Distributed Deep Learning for Joint Resource Orchestration in 6G Extreme Edge Computing), RANControl (Reinforced Structural Learning-based xApps for O-RAN Closed-loop Control), and FedHea (Few-Shot Federated Learning with Variance Reduction for Ransomware Attack Detection in IoHTs).

UDL Module Intervention N-TUTORR Poster Presentation · ATU

N-TUTORR UDL Plus-One Multimodal Content ATU Donegal
Enhancing AI through Multimodal Content: Plus-one Approach to UDL
N-TUTORR Poster Presentation · ATU Donegal · 2025
Dr. Henna presented a research poster at the N-TUTORR (National Transformation of Undergraduate Teaching, Online and Research) showcase at ATU, demonstrating the application of Universal Design for Learning principles to AI teaching through a Plus-One approach to UDL intervention.

The research, conducted at ATU Donegal (supervisors: Loise McGinty, Patricia Brennan, and Dr. Deirdre McClay), examined how UDL-aligned multimodal content enhances student engagement and inclusion in AI modules. Key findings showed that:
  • Interactive UDL elements significantly increased student engagement and learning confidence
  • Multimodal representations addressed the diverse needs of international and neurodiverse students
  • The Plus-One approach to UDL positively impacted professional development as an educator
  • Accommodation-to-accessibility shift reduced language barriers for ESL students
